speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a 34-year-old male with a history of AIDS presenting with decreased vision and floaters in your right eye. To begin, are you experiencing any floaters, flashes of light, or a curtain-like shadow in your vision?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is concerning; given your history of AIDS, Kaposi's sarcoma, and fungal esophagitis, this could indicate an opportunistic ocular infection. Have you noticed any floaters, flashes of light, or a dark curtain blocking part of your vision?

REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy
REQUEST IMAGES: Fundus_photo_right_eye

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis

The fundoscopy findings of granular yellow-white opacities and dot-blot hemorrhages in your right eye are highly characteristic of CMV retinitis, a serious opportunistic infection common in AIDS patients. We need to urgently assess your viral load and CD4 count to guide treatment, but this condition requires immediate antiviral therapy.
